websiteToolCalorieDeficit.title: Calorie deficit and goal date calculator
websiteToolCalorieDeficit.intro: Set a goal weight and a date to see the daily calorie target that gets you there, the range it sits in and whether the pace is realistic.

problems.height: Enter a height within the range the calculator accepts.
problems.weight: Enter a weight within the range the calculator accepts.
problems.goalWeight: Enter a goal weight within the range the calculator accepts.
problems.goalDateNotFuture: The goal date must be after today.

results.share: Deficit as a share of daily energy use

notes.noChange: You are already at that weight, so no change is needed.
notes.floor: Your target would be below the minimum of {{floor}}, so the page sets it there.
notes.laterDate: The earliest date that minimum allows is {{date}}.
notes.floorAboveTdee: Estimated energy use is at or below the minimum, so no deficit is possible. Choose a higher goal weight or talk to a clinician.
notes.pace: This pace is above 1% of your body weight per week, a Musclog guideline. A slower pace usually holds up better.
notes.deficitLarge: This deficit is above 25% of your estimated energy use, a Musclog guideline. A smaller deficit over a longer time is usually easier to keep.
notes.range: The estimate is uncertain, so the target is shown as a range: 10% of your energy use either side. The 10% is a Musclog product choice, not a measured error.
notes.thresholds: The 1% pace and 25% deficit guidelines are Musclog product choices, not findings from a study.

sections.title: How the target is made
body: Your energy use is estimated from your sex, age, height and weight (the Mifflin-St Jeor resting rate) multiplied by your activity level. It is the same estimate the Musclog app uses when it has no tracking history.

The weight change is turned into energy with the app's kilocalories-per-kilogram rule and spread across the days to your goal date. The target is that energy use minus the daily deficit (or plus, for a gain).

sections.title: Why the date is a guide
body: Hall et al. (2011) modelled how body weight responds to a change in energy intake. The body adjusts over months, so a fixed number of calories per kilogram is an approximation. Weigh yourself every few weeks and adjust.

sections.title: The minimum
body: The target never goes below the minimum the app uses: 1,200 kcal for women and 1,500 kcal for men, or 80% of your resting rate if that is higher. If your date needs less, the page gives the earliest date the minimum allows.

sources.hall: Hall et al. (2011), quantification of the effect of energy imbalance on body weight
